messages:
maria (Support): Heads-up — enterprise customer (org-678) reports big p95 latency and intermittent 503s when targeting EU models. They say traffic is landing in us-east-1 despite pinning to eu-west-1.
julie (Customer): confirmed. Started ~2026-03-16 09:12 UTC. Some requests succeed but many are 503s or 200 with +350ms extra RTT. header shows X-Redwood-Served-Region: us-east-1 even though our integration set region=eu-west-1.
ops-bot: alert: route-divergence detected org=678 spillover=true capacity.eu-west-1=94% capacity.us-east-1=72%
alex (SRE): Can you paste one request ID and the headers? Also ping/span IDs if available.
julie (Customer): req id: r-0a4f2e8c; trace: trace-9c3; headers: 
  x-api-key: ****
  x-client-region: eu-west-1
  x-redwood-expected-region: eu-west-1
  response header: x-redwood-served-region: us-east-1
maria (Support): Repro steps from customer (they ran locally):
  curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" \\  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
  -> got 503, headers show served-region us-east-1.
ingrid (Routing): quick triage: looks like autospillover was triggered on eu-west due to high queue length. But routing should honor per-org pinning. Two possibilities: (1) pin records stale/evicted and system applied spillover; (2) sticky routing cache has stale node mapping that prefers us-east.
alex (SRE): I pulled route-proxy logs for r-0a4f2e8c: 
```
2026-03-16T09:12:42Z route-proxy[router-5] INFO org=678 req=r-0a4f2e8c incoming_region=eu-west-1 capacity_eu=94 spillover_threshold=90 decision=spillover_target=us-east-1 reason="queue_depth>threshold && fallback_policy=allow_cross_region"
2026-03-16T09:12:42Z route-proxy[router-5] DEBUG pin-check org=678 pin_record=missing cached_sticky=us-east-1
```
alex (SRE): so the proxy couldn't find a valid pin_record and fell back to cached_sticky which pointed to us-east. That cached mapping persisted and we didn't re-evaluate after capacity dipped.
maria (Support): How did pin_record go missing? token scope should have created a persistent pin during onboarding.
ingrid (Routing): hypothesis: pin records are stored in redis with TTL 30d but a deployment that migrated route metadata earlier this week accidentally set TTLs to 0 for a subset of orgs. I see a migration job that touched org-6** namespace.
ops-bot: deploy: migration-job-restore-routing ran 2026-03-14T02:11:08Z status=complete
alex (SRE): Confirmed with redis: `GET routing:pin:org:678` -> nil. But `GET routing:sticky:org:678` -> "us-east-1".
alex (SRE): Quick mitigation: set a temporary override to force eu-west for org-678 and clear sticky cache. Commands I ran: 
```
# force pin
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \\
  https://internal-api.redwood/v1/route/pin -d '{"org":"678","region":"eu-west-1","reason":"support emergency"}'
# clear cached sticky
redis-cli DEL routing:sticky:org:678
```
alex (SRE): After override, I spun a small canary policy to avoid immediate spillover until capacity settles: applied routes/overrides/org-678.yaml (canary).
maria (Support): Customer testing now?
julie (Customer): retested at 09:28 UTC — looks much better. p95 back to expected range, no 503s for last 5 minutes. THANKS.
ingrid (Routing): Root cause timeline: migration-job unexpectedly zeroed TTLs for a batch of pin records on 2026-03-14; when pins expired, sticky caches filled with last-known served-region (us-east) and stayed until manually cleared. With eu-west hitting temporary 94% utilization, proxy followed fallback_policy and sent traffic to us-east.
alex (SRE): Action items:
- [P1] Restore pin records from backup and remove incorrect migration (ingrid) — target 2026-03-16 13:00 UTC
- [P2] Add safeguard to migration tool to never set TTL < 7d for routing pins (eng-infra)
- [P2] Add metric/alert for pin TTL drops and for sticky cache hit-rate anomalies (sre)
- [P3] Postmortem + notify customer billing team — potential cross-region egress billing spike (finance)
maria (Support): I've opened ticket 78921 and told customer we'll follow up with timeline and billing check.
julie (Customer): one more ask — can you confirm whether any requests were reprocessed or double-billed? We saw a small usage spike.
alex (SRE): We're checking backend request ingest logs for duplication. Initial look: no duplicate request IDs. Likely just egress cost due to cross-region serving. We'll include numbers in follow-up.
ingrid (Routing): I'll push the restore job now (incidents/restore-pin-org-678). Also adding a temporary stricter fallback for enterprise-locked orgs to prefer local region until health stabilizes.
ops-bot: job incidents/restore-pin-org-678 started by ingrid at 2026-03-16T10:04:12Z
ops-bot: job incidents/restore-pin-org-678 completed status=success duration=2m34s
alex (SRE): Verified `GET routing:pin:org:678` -> eu-west-1; sticky cache cleared. Sampling traces show served-region eu-west-1 for recent requests.
maria (Support): Customer confirmation: julie — can you confirm 24h and if billing numbers look OK?
julie (Customer): confirmed — latency stable, no 503s in last hour. We'll review billing and escalate if needed.
alex (SRE): Follow-ups: I'll add an automated reconciliation to compare pin versus sticky caches and alert when >1% mismatch across orgs.
ingrid (Routing): Will add migration guard rails.
maria (Support): Closing thread once billing check done. Add this to postmortem queue. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
